clue.text: Horrify a withdrawn Scandinavian

indicators.note: withdrawn, read as drawn back, tells us to turn the Scandinavian's letters round

parts.note: a Lapp is a Sami person from the north of Scandinavia

explanation.surface: Someone shocks a shy, retiring Scandinavian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' looks like a description of a shy person, but read as drawn back it turns the Scandinavian round. A Lapp is a reindeer-herding Sami from the far north.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to fill them with dismay or shock, a synonym of horrify.

clue.text: Declare that a couple of Poles carry little weight

indicators.note: couple of asks for two of the pole letter, side by side

parts.note: N stands for the north pole
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone states that two Polish people can hardly carry anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland; it is the geographic pole, N.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to make something known publicly, a synonym of declare.

clue.text: Frantic stop-over in East Germany

indicators.note: over says the run of words is turned back to front

parts.note: mad means frantic or wild

explanation.surface: A frenzied break in a journey through eastern Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop-over' looks like a break in a journey, but 'over' reverses MAD STOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Potsdam is a city near Berlin, in what was East Germany, defined by its location.

clue.text: Use it to fry the French way

parts.note: la is a French word for the
Rd abbreviates road, a way

explanation.surface: A tip on frying food as the French cook do it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lard is pig fat used as a cooking fat for frying.

clue.text: Correct a cool-headed cleric

indicators.note: cool-headed is read as the head of the word cool, its opening letter only

parts.note: a curate is an assistant member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A clergyman who keeps calm is praised as being right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cool-headed' looks like a description of the cleric's temperament; it gives only C, the head of 'cool'.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate and correct are synonyms: both mean free from error.

clue.text: Pet lions cannot be set free. Capital!

indicators.note: be set free says the letters are released into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A warning that pet lions must not be released, with an exclamation of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like an exclamation meaning excellent; it is the definition, the old name of a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantinople, now Istanbul, was the capital of the Byzantine and Ottoman empires.

clue.text: Impulse felt by a childless operator

indicators.note: childless means lacking a son, so the boy is removed from the word

parts.note: a surgeon operates on patients

explanation.surface: A doctor without children feels a strong longing.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong desire or drive, a synonym of impulse.

clue.text: Appearance of a royal contender

parts.note: R abbreviates royal, as in RN for Royal Navy
a rival is a competitor or contender

explanation.surface: A competitor for the throne turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrival is someone or something turning up, so it is an appearance.

clue.text: Antelope from an oriental country

parts.note: E stands for east, the orient
land is a synonym of country

explanation.surface: An antelope comes from a nation in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns.

clue.text: Inform how to finish the game

explanation.surface: A referee explains how to end a match by telling.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow the whistle is idiom for exposing wrongdoing; a referee also sounds the whistle to end a match.

clue.text: Unsophisticated old city in S African province

indicators.note: in places the old city inside the name of the province

parts.note: Natal was a province of South Africa
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An ancient city is described as rustic and located in a South African region.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural behaviour is artless and unaffected, so it can mean unsophisticated.

clue.text: Grain that is produced in Africa

indicators.note: produced suggests the letters are worked up into something new

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A cereal crop is grown on the African continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigeria is a West African country, so the clue defines it by its location on that continent.

clue.text: Your duty includes communication in Pakistan

indicators.note: includes says the answer sits inside the words your duty

explanation.surface: Part of your obligation is to talk to people in Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, a means of communication there.

clue.text: They're foolish taunts

explanation.surface: Mockers who jeer are silly people.
explanation.definitionFit: Twits are fools or idiots; to twit someone is to tease or mock them, so twits are also jibes.

clue.text: Eager for sextet to appear in commercial

indicators.note: to appear in puts the six inside the advertisement

parts.note: an ad is a commercial advertisement
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone is keen for a six-piece band to feature in a television advert.
explanation.definitionFit: Avid means keen or enthusiastic, a synonym of eager.

clue.text: Opportunity for judge to imprison ringleader

indicators.note: to imprison puts the leader of the ring inside the judge

parts.note: beak is British slang for a magistrate or judge
the leader of the word ring is its first letter

explanation.surface: A chance for a magistrate to lock up the chief troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A break is a lucky chance, as in a big break.

clue.text: I have to put in the right bolt

indicators.note: to put in places the contraction inside the abbreviation

parts.note: RT abbreviates right
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone must install a proper fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivet is a metal pin for fastening plates together, a kind of bolt.

clue.text: Understandable resolution of Chinese problem

indicators.note: resolution of suggests breaking the words up and solving them into a new order

explanation.surface: Solving a problem from China makes it intelligible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolution of' looks like solving a puzzle but rearranges CHINESE PROBLEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comprehensible can be grasped by the mind, so it is understandable.

clue.text: Let out and let out again

explanation.surface: Something is freed and then rented again.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the second as RE-LEASED: rented out once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Released means freed; re-leased means leased or rented out once more.

clue.text: Only he is trusted to fulfil the European dream

definitions.text: Only he is trusted to fulfil the European dream

parts.words: Only he is trusted to fulfil the European dream
parts.note: European is read as white, a champion of the white race on whom all expectations rest

explanation.surface: A single person is relied on to make Europe's ambition real.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase originated in boxing, for white fighters hoped to beat the black champion Jack Johnson; it now means anyone expected to bring great success.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a figure is the one person on whom a group pins its hopes of victory.

clue.text: Stress that the lost sheep has been found?

definitions.text: the lost sheep has been found?

explanation.surface: A shepherd emphasises the stray sheep's return.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical second reading: the male sheep is back home.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram home is idiom for emphasising a point; literally a ram returned home is a found sheep.

clue.text: Tyrannize journalists after work

indicators.note: after places the reporters behind the piece of work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Reporters bully people after finishing work.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to rule cruelly or keep down by force, a synonym of tyrannize.

clue.text: Drag one's feet if lacking energy

explanation.surface: Someone shuffles along when they feel tired.
explanation.definitionFit: To limp is to walk lamely, dragging a leg; limp as an adjective means floppy or feeble.

clue.text: Pound sign

explanation.surface: The symbol for the British currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra is the Latin pound, source of lb; it is also a zodiac sign, the scales.

clue.text: Suddenly discover how to continue batting

explanation.surface: A batsman realises in a flash how to keep scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit on an idea is to find it by chance; a batsman who hits on keeps striking the ball and stays in.

clue.text: Some of the chaps ended up in church

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Several of the men finished their journey at a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ended up' looks like one phrase, but ENDED gives the final E and 'up in church' places the recess at the altar end.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the vaulted recess at the east end of a church, beyond the choir, so it is up in church.

clue.text: He said history was bunk. That's shallow

explanation.surface: A famous dismissal of the past is called superficial.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Ford, the carmaker, famously said history was bunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Ford made that remark; a ford is a shallow place where a river can be crossed.

clue.text: A strange plant

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: Someone describes an odd plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum is a plant, such as the arum lily, with a hooded spathe.

clue.text: Huge meal must mean a spare tyre!

explanation.surface: Overeating at a feast leads to a roll of fat round the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spare tyre' is slang for belly fat, which a huge meal suggests; but a burst tyre also needs the spare.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowout is slang for a lavish feast and also a sudden puncture of a tyre, after which the spare is fitted.

clue.text: Bounty was a big boat

parts.note: large is a synonym of big
SS stands for steamship, a common abbreviation for a boat

explanation.surface: The Bounty, the famous mutiny ship, was a large vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounty' looks like the name of the ship from the famous mutiny; it is the definition, meaning generosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving of gifts or money, which is bounty in its sense of liberality.

clue.text: Bread is made even in Scotland

indicators.note: is made suggests the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: Bread is baked smooth north of the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland, defined by where it lies.

clue.text: Contemplated Frenchman being exploited

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a French man's title
used means exploited or taken advantage of

explanation.surface: A man from France pondered being taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or reflect, so mused means contemplated.
